newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Randgold says listing "satisfactory" after Bre-X.
newsitem.headline: Randgold says listing "satisfactory" after Bre-X.

text.p: Randgold and Exploration Company Ltd said on Thursday the listing of its exploration arm Randgold Resources on the London Stock Exchange was satisfactory in the light of the Bre-X scandal and other negative market factors.
The company confirmed in a statement that Randgold Resources' offer price on the LSE was set at $16.50 and the size of the offer was 5 million shares -- instead of the expected 7 million.
It said conditional dealings in the shares started on the LSE on Thursday afternoon with unconditional listing and dealings set for July 1.
Randgold Resources managing director Mark Bristow said the price and size of the offer did not meet the ambitious targets the company had set for itself.
But he added: "The outcome was satisfactory considering the adverse circumstances which had developed since it had embarked on this exercise".

Bristow cited gold's downturn to below $340 an ounce, the continuing impact on investors of the Bre-X scandal, where a Canadian junior exploration company vastly overstated the potential of a gold find in Indonesia, and the general state of the major capital markets.

He said the $82.5 million proceeds from the offering will go towards funding the capital expenditure programme at the firm's Syama gold mine in Mali and repayment of a loan assumed when it bought Syama last year.
It would also be used to develop the Loulo mine in Mali and pay for a bankable feasibility study for the Golden Ridge project in Tanzania.
"In addition, it will fund our ongoing exploration programme," Bristow said.
He said the company now had a market capitalisation of $327 million -- based on the offer price.
